subject: Request: Senior approval for Hosted API pricing concession for MedAtlas
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0000
Subject: Request: Senior approval for Hosted API pricing concession for MedAtlas

Team —

Quick summary: MedAtlas (legacy on-prem customer) is ready to convert a large portion of their NLU pipelines to our Hosted API. They signed the NDA last week and want a single-year commercial to ease migration risk. Commercial ask: 30% off list Hosted API usage rate for the first 12 months (they requested 35% but indicated 40% as an anchor). They are asking for the concession to be applied to all token consumption (ingest + generation) and for credits to cover an initial onboarding spike.

Why this matters:
- Expected starting consumption: ~1.1–1.4B tokens/month once pipelines cut over.
- Pro forma run-rate at list: ~$135k/mo in recurring usage revenue ( ~ $1.62M ARR ).
- With 30% concession that becomes ~$94.5k/mo; revenue shift is material to our hosted unit economics but keeps a marquee customer on hosted.
- They are strategic: large potential Dedicated upsell in 12–18 months, strong reference for payer/health vertical.

Request: senior approval to offer 30% off Hosted API usage for months 0–12, plus a one-time $50k onboarding credit (applied as invoice credit). This exceeds our normal authorized discount band for Hosted (standard cap 20%).

Conditions I recommend if approved:
1) Commit clause: customer must commit to minimum 6 months of production usage; early termination triggers clawback of onboarding credit pro-rata.
2) Auto-evaluate for Dedicated: if average monthly tokens > 2B for two consecutive months, commercial switches to Dedicated list rates with migration support.
3) Legal to add explicit data residency + audit-logs appendix (Rafael).
4) Finance signoff on P&L impact (Aditya).

Attachments: pricing calc and NDA. HubSpot deal DL-4582 has the SOW draft.

Asking for a decision by end of day tomorrow (Thu) so sales can lock commercial and DocuSign. If we cannot approve >=25% they may walk to a competitor.

Thanks,
Markus
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MedAtlas_PRICING_CALC.xlsx (xlsx), MedAtlas_Signed_NDA.pdf (pdf)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Request: Senior approval for Hosted API pricing concession for MedAtlas

Markus / Mina —

Adding commercial context: MedAtlas is migrating two major NLP pipelines (claims triage + coding). Their renewal window is Q3; this conversion is the easiest path to establish usage anchor. They sign faster if we can match the effective rate they're used to under their legacy vendor.

Impact scenarios (rounded):
- No concession: ~ $135k/mo net (annualized $1.62M).
- 20% concession: ~$108k/mo ($1.3M ARR).
- 30% concession: ~$95k/mo ($1.14M ARR).

Our preferred middle ground if we need to be more conservative: 25% discount + $75k onboarding credits (reduces near-term revenue impact and helps with churn risk).

Commercial asks we need answered from execs:
- Approve concession band (25–30%)
- Approve onboarding credit up to $75k
- Approve auto-migration clause to Dedicated if usage spikes above threshold

If approved we'll move DocuSign and lock a 12mo term with an explicit usage minimum. I'm in favor of the 30% for 12 months if Legal and Finance accept the conditions — we capture the customer and materially increase likelihood of Dedicated adoption.

Karthik
Senior Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: Senior approval for Hosted API pricing concession for MedAtlas

Folks —

Legal's perspective: we can accept a pricing concession, but need to protect data residency and limit long-term precedent. Two quick asks before I can sign off:

1) Add a one-year clause that makes the concession explicit to months 0–12 and states that thereafter customer resumes standard rates unless a new approved concession is signed. This avoids open-ended precedence.
2) Include an audit right and additional security appendix referencing SOC 2 evidence (they already received SOC 2 report in NDA exchange). We'll need one extra clause on egress controls for PII pipelines.

Also, we should avoid blanket token coverage for onboarding spikes — limit onboarding credit to ingestion-related pre-prod spikes and cap usage credit to the first 90 days (keeps cost bounded).

If Sales wants to go above 30% I need exec approval in writing; I recommend 30% cap for legal acceptance.

Rafael
Head of Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: Senior approval for Hosted API pricing concession for MedAtlas

Thanks all for the clear write-up. I approve a 30% Hosted API usage concession for months 0–12 and a one-time $50k onboarding credit under the following non-negotiable conditions:

1) Concession explicitly timeboxed to first 12 months in SOW; no dilution to future pricing precedent.
2) Onboarding credit limited to the first 90 days and tied to defined onboarding milestones; early termination triggers pro-rata clawback.
3) Legal to add data residency + audit-logs appendix and SCIM/SAML requirements in the SOW.
4) Finance (Aditya) to confirm accounting treatment and expected QoQ revenue impact; bookings must reflect net-of-credit terms.
5) Include an auto-evaluate clause: if rolling 30-day average tokens > 2B for 2 consecutive months, we trigger a migration path to Dedicated with migration credits to be negotiated by Sales.

Markus — proceed to update the SOW and send DocuSign with the conditions above. Accounting: please prepare the invoice schedule and credit treatment. Legal: please provide the exact appendix language and confirm.

Mina
President, Commercial
Redwood Inference
